Statement



                        H.E. Zoran Zaev

  President of the Government of the Republic of Macedonia


                    72th Session of the

             United Nations General Assembly
                     Plenary Meeting


Mr. Secretary General,

Mr. President

Ladies and Gentlemen,
Distinguished Excellencies,


Dear Colleagues,


I have the honor to address  this important forum and to share with you the
positions of the Republic of Macedonia on the most important issues on the United
Nations’ agenda.


Tam convinced that we have the same goal: world peace.
Iam convinced that we share the same commitments: decent life for all ina

sustainable environment.
Tam convinced that we will find common solutions to our common challenges.


Peace, the commitment for decent life and joint solutions are the values that
Republic of Macedonia used to overcome a deep political crisis that sent waves
throughout our region.


We area  small country fill with diversity. We managed to overcome difficult
challenges because we united around common values. This is why the Republic of
Macedonia today is again free, secure and stable. Republic of Macedonia is a friend
with all of its neighbors and is firmly oriented toward full integration in NATO and

EU.


As Head of the Delegation of the Republic of Macedonia,  I want to congratulate His
Excellency Miroslav Lajcak of the Slovak Republic on his election to the prestigious
position of President of the Seventy Second Session of the UN General Assembly.

I would also like to express our full support to Secretary General Guterres. We wish
him much success in carrying through his comprehensive and ambitious, but very
much needed agenda for transformation and adjustment of the United Nations to
the demanding tasks and our common existing and emerging challenges.


UN must continue to do more and better to meet those challenges and stand the
test of time. We must be vigilant and sustained, but also provide innovative and
adaptable conflict prevention, sustainable development and management reform
mechanisms, while building on the foundations enshrined in the UN Charter and
other core documents.


Mr. President,


The world is plagued by severe humanitarian crisis, protracted and new conflicts,
intensification of terrorist attacks and violent extremism, human rights abuses and
increasing climate change effects.

Different in scope and weight, those challenges become more complex. They require
a wide-ranging response. While we were able to mitigate the consequences for
some, others remain unabated.


Just a few weeks ago we witnessed devastating natural disasters in the Mexican
Gulf and South Asia. This is a harsh reminder that our Planet is altering and we all
have an obligation  to do our best  to mitigate, and hopefully even revert the
consequences. We can progress if we are united.


Mr. President,


Promotion and protection of human rights, democracy and the rule of law must
remain at the core of our action. Despite the fact that the UN has a robust human
rights architecture, the current blatant human rights violations around the globe,
widespread impunity and lack of accountability, remind us that there is much to be
done.


Monstrous terrorist attacks have increased. Our actions must focus on prevention
of violent extremism and radicalization as major factors for terrorist recruitment.
The establishment of the new structure of the UN Office for Countering Terrorism
where one of the priorities areas is prevention was a welcome step. On our part, we
also work on a national strategy on the prevention of violent extremism and
radicalization.

                                I am aware that there are different approaches to this crucial issue, as we have
                divergent views on many others. However, I would like to urge you not to focus on
                our differences, but on our primary responsibilities to act robustly for the common
                   benefit.

              The proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery
                continues to jeopardize global security. The implementation of the UN Security
                 Council resolution 1540 is key to minimize possible disastrous consequences for the
                generations to come. In that regard, let me underline that we are deeply alarmed by
                the continued unilateral actions of the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. They
                conduct nuclear tests and missile launches despite the repeated  calls by the
                 international community to fully comply with the relevant United Nations Security
                 Council  resolutions. We  believe  that peaceful  denuclearisation  of the Korean
                peninsula is a viable avenue and therefore urge the Democratic People's Republic of
               Korea to immediately abandon its nuclear and missile programs and to sign and
                   ratify the Comprehensive Nuclear Ban Test Treaty.




                 Mr. President,

                 Let me briefly comment on the main theme of the 72"? UNGA debate” Focusing on
                  people: Striving for peace and a decent life for all on a sustainable planet”.


                 States must remain focused on  the implementation  of the new  sustainable
               development agenda we agreed at the 70" Anniversary of our Organization. This
                remarkable undertaking laid the foundations for future development framework.
                 This has implications on many other important areas of common concern.


             Many vital issues for global prosperity are related to its implementation. Therefore,
                         it is important to continue to encourage and build new avenues of cooperation and
             new partnerships among us. This  is central for the integration of the economic,
               environmental and social dimensions of sustainability. This is the fundamentals for
               development, a hopeful future, and our peace, stability and security.


             On national level, our efforts to transform into practice agreed goals are included in
                 the new UNDAF program entitled “Partnership for Sustainable Development: UN
                Strategy 2016-2020”.

               Allow me  to  refer  to the  last year important Summit on the issue of large
             movements of refugees and migrants. This  is a global phenomenon, caused by
                  different reasons, with diverse implications. The UN adopted a comprehensive

                    political  declaration  and  pledged  to  intensify  international  cooperation,  in
                  particular among the countries of origin or nationality, transit and destination.

              The Republic of Macedonia supports and takes part in the ongoing consultations
                processes on the two compacts: refugees and migrants. We expect an outcome that
                    will address  all aspects of the global phenomena. Let me remind you that last
                couple of years hundreds of thousands of migrants transited through my country
               and the region. Even though we faced complex challenges at that time, we managed
                  to provide humanitarian assistance to the people in need.


                 Mr. President,


              As we have to adapt globally, we must also do homework and act as responsible
               governments to secure and provide better future and prosperity to our people.


              The Government  of  the  Republic  of Macedonia  confirms  its  dedication  to
               fundamental democratic values, good governance, rule of law and the respect of
             human rights. We overcame a deep political and institutional crisis through our
                  resolute  stand  in defense  of these fundamentals. Our understanding  is  that
              democracy needs to be driven by civic engagement from bottom up. Societies are
                 better off when decision-making  is a comprehensive, inclusive and transparent.
                  Public policies need to work for citizens’ well-being.


           My government has laid out an ambitious reform plan, 3-6-9 Plan, with short,
             medium  and  long-term  measures.  Our  goal  is  to  restore  democracy,  build
                 professional and independent institutions and improve the standard of living for
               each citizen. Our aim is to expedite the integration of Republic of Macedonia into
            EU and NATO.


              From the depths of the political crisis we emerged stronger and we were able to
                 contribute to regional stability and regional cooperation. Those of you that know
               Balkan history, know that our region was not always labelled positively.  I strongly
                 believe that we have a new chance to make a change ~ not only in perceptions, but
                   in substance. Over the past few months, the Government of Republic of Macedonia
                has strongly promoted a new approach to our neighbors. We demonstrated capacity
                  to overcome open issues. We articulated and acted on our national interests. At the
              same time, we were fully aware and respectful of the national interests of our
                 neighbors. Our policy is based on solving issues through dialogue and cooperation.
          We hope that it can inspire others and incite new approach to bilateral relations in
                our region.

As a positive step forward let me underscore the signing of a bilateral agreement
on friendship, good-neighborliness and cooperation with Bulgaria. This is a joint
success of the two countries.


This General Assembly is the 25" participation of the Republic of Macedonia, as an
independent state. Next year, we will be marking a quarter of century of our UN
membership. However, this anniversary is also marked with the dispute over how
my country should be referred to. This dispute has unilateral consequences to our
development and perspectives.


The Interim Agreement of 1995 laid the foundations to normalize relations between
Macedonia and Greece. At present the two countries are implementing confidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
building measures. This is a very positive development. We have a fresh impetus to                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
overcome the long-standing bilateral dispute.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |


I would say we both made certain mistakes at different times, but the main goal
now is to close the issue.  | firmly believe that we must seize the momentum, discuss
in bona fide and resolve the issue for our shared future. We highly value the
continuous  efforts  of the  Personal Envoy  of the UN Secretary  General  His
Excellency, Mr. Matthew Nimetz and the good offices he provides to that end.  |
firmly believe that there is a way to overcome the problem that Greece has with our
constitutional name. For a change, let us try to approach it from a positive point of
view.


Maintaining good neighborly and friendly relations is a two-way avenue. We are
committed to do our job and expect the same of our neighbors. This message was
already clearly sent to our friends and partners. I would like to reaffirm it here, from
this podium, where all of us are recalling the Universal Charter’s principles and
goals.


Mr. President,


The World can be a very noisy place, but the most important things in the World
can be very quiet.  I believe that if we listen to our people, then we can hear the
World.


In conclusion,   | want to underline that the Republic  of Macedonia remains a
staunch supporter of multilateralism. We will continue to work with you and with
all UN Member States on jointly reinforcing world peace and security, on promoting
human rights, on achieving the sustainable development goals and on all other
issues that are crucial for the people we represent.  | thank you.
